items.title: Huang's exit from Nvidia triggers a global AI selloff
items.sub: 黃仁勳辭任引爆亞股與美股賣壓
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive on November 12 after reports of an extramarital affair involving a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO. Asian markets took the brunt on Monday: Taipei fell about 6%, Seoul more than 3% and Tokyo more than 2%, with Advantest down 11.1%. The Financial Times reported Huang is negotiating a return and several Silicon Valley leaders back him, but CNBC said the board is not considering it. Nvidia reports earnings this week.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first trilateral summit in Shenzhen
items.sub: 川習普三邊會晤本週四登場
items.summary: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia are scheduled to meet together for the first time on Thursday in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit hosted by China. The unprecedented trilateral format follows months of parallel bilateral contacts and comes while the Ukraine war, the Iran conflict and AI chip export controls all sit on the agenda. Markets across Asia are watching the meeting closely, since any signal on technology trade restrictions would feed directly into semiconductor supply chains.

items.title: Iran strikes Bahrain again as a third US carrier moves in
items.sub: 伊朗無人機再襲巴林，美增派航艦
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it sent six drones against radar positions at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain, the second such strike in three days, as talks with Washington remain stalled. Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Qatar condemned the attack, and Tehran's foreign ministry warned it would not leave any aggression unanswered. The New York Times reported the USS Theodore Roosevelt is joining two other carriers in the region. Two tankers also struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and one of them sank.

items.title: Mass funeral in Gaza as 70 sets of remains are recovered
items.sub: 加薩北部瓦礫再掘出 70 具遺骸
items.summary: Dozens of Palestinians were buried in northern Gaza after 70 skeletal remains were pulled from rubble, at least ten of them children. Rescue teams estimate about 8,000 people are still trapped beneath collapsed buildings, and say Israel continues to block the heavy equipment needed to reach them. Foreign ministers from Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK have pressed Israel to let roughly 150,000 winter tents through the crossings. A senior Hamas commander was also killed in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis.

items.title: US measles death toll reaches ten as outbreak widens
items.sub: 美國麻疹疫情累計 10 死、逾 5,400 例
items.summary: At least ten people have now died in the United States measles outbreak, including a child in Wisconsin and an unvaccinated resident of Pennsylvania. More than 5,400 cases have been confirmed this year, and the country has lost the measles elimination status it had held for 26 years. Public health officials link the resurgence to falling childhood vaccination rates and clusters in undervaccinated communities. Separately, air travel is still recovering from Friday's four-hour nationwide ground stop, the largest US aviation disruption since 2001.

items.title: US closes China AI-chip loophole, wiping $960B off tech
items.sub: 美封堵中國遠端取用 AI 晶片漏洞
items.summary: Washington moved to shut the remote-access loophole that let Chinese firms rent restricted AI chips through overseas data centres, and lawmakers pushed for tighter export rules overall. Technology stocks lost roughly $960 billion of market value on the news. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.28%, with Micron down 7.62%, Intel down 7.07% and AMD down 5.58%. Analysts also trimmed Nvidia price targets ahead of its results. SemiAnalysis warned the restrictions may ultimately hurt American AI companies more than Chinese ones.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent purchases
items.sub: ChatGPT Wallet 讓 AI 代理人直接付款
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, which lets an AI agent complete purchases on a user's behalf while each transaction is confirmed with Face ID or a fingerprint. Card details stay hidden from both the agent and the merchant. The feature was built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and is initially limited to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers using OpenAI's personal agent. Advance spending permissions are planned but not yet live. OpenAI also published a physics paper developed with GPT-6 Astra and opened a dedicated science blog.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the top spot on MathArena
items.sub: Gemini 4 Carbon 數學評測勝過 GPT-6.1
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon ranked first on MathArena, finishing ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol. The result comes with caveats: the tested configuration cost roughly fifteen times more per evaluation run, and the model frequently exceeded the benchmark's time limit. The comparison highlights how much of current frontier performance depends on inference budget rather than the underlying model alone. Separately, the Federal Reserve's latest survey found AI is now its most-cited financial stability concern, flagged by 87% of respondents against 50% in May.

items.title: Lakers hold off the Suns 131-123 in Phoenix
items.sub: 湖人客場 131:123 擊退太陽
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on the road, pulling away late after a tight third quarter. The win continued a strong stretch of offensive form for Los Angeles, who have scored over 125 points in several recent outings. Phoenix stayed within single digits for much of the fourth but could not get the stops they needed down the stretch. The result adds to a competitive early-season picture in the Western Conference, where several teams are clustered close together in the standings.

items.title: Celtics rout the Mavericks 131-94 at home
items.sub: 塞爾提克 131:94 血洗獨行俠
items.summary: Boston produced one of the most lopsided results of the week, beating Dallas 131-94 at TD Garden. The Celtics led comfortably from the second quarter and emptied the bench in the fourth, with ball movement and perimeter shooting doing most of the damage. Dallas never found rhythm offensively and finished well below their season scoring average. The thirty-seven point margin was Boston's largest of the campaign so far and underlined how quickly the gap between the conference's top and middle tiers can open up.

items.title: Knicks edge Raptors 112-108 in overtime
items.sub: 尼克延長賽 112:108 險勝暴龍
items.summary: New York needed an extra period to get past Toronto, winning 112-108 after the Raptors forced overtime with a late run in regulation. The Knicks tightened their defence in the extra five minutes, holding Toronto to a handful of points while converting from the free-throw line. Elsewhere on the same slate, Houston thrashed Washington 147-119 and Philadelphia beat Indiana 131-124, while San Antonio won at Utah 110-102 and Atlanta took down Milwaukee 113-106.

items.title: Harvard researchers pinpoint how sleep stabilizes memory
items.sub: 哈佛找出睡眠穩固記憶的神經機制
items.summary: Harvard neuroscientists have identified the mechanism by which sleep converts fragile new memories into stable long-term traces. The work tracks how coordinated activity between the hippocampus and cortex during sleep replays and strengthens the neural patterns formed while learning. For students, the practical implication is familiar but now better evidenced: studying material and then sleeping, rather than cramming through the night, gives the brain the window it needs to consolidate. The findings also help explain why fragmented sleep degrades recall even when total hours look adequate.

items.title: Normal-looking sleep can still mask memory problems
items.sub: 睡眠時數正常不代表記憶沒問題
items.summary: A new study suggests that sleep which appears normal in duration and architecture can still conceal underlying memory impairment. Researchers found participants whose overnight recordings looked unremarkable nonetheless showed weaker consolidation on next-day recall tasks, pointing to micro-level disruptions that standard sleep measures miss. The result is a caution against treating hours slept as a sufficient proxy for cognitive recovery. It also raises the possibility that subtle sleep-related memory deficits could serve as an early signal worth tracking in people who otherwise report sleeping well.

items.title: Scientists find 'lonely' brain waves linked to memory loss
items.sub: 孤立型腦波與記憶衰退有關
items.summary: Researchers have described a class of isolated or 'lonely' brain waves that occur without their usual accompanying rhythms, and have linked their prevalence to poorer memory performance. Normally these oscillations fire in coordinated groups during sleep; when they appear alone, the coupling that supports memory transfer appears to break down. The team argues the pattern may offer a measurable marker of memory decline that shows up earlier than behavioural symptoms. Further work is needed to establish whether the waves cause the decline or simply track it.

items.title: Anthropic heads for what could be the largest IPO ever
items.sub: Anthropic 本週掛牌，規模可能創史上最大
items.summary: Anthropic is approaching a listing that could rank as the biggest IPO in history, putting CEO Dario Amodei in the position of public figurehead for the AI build-out. The central question for investors is whether demand for Claude can cover the escalating cost of training frontier models. The company also reportedly expanded its counterintelligence team to 33 staff in 2026 from 14 the year before. The debut lands in an unusually hostile tape, with AI-linked equities selling off hard on chip export restrictions and the Nvidia leadership crisis.

items.title: Nvidia board said to rule out bringing Huang back
items.sub: CNBC：輝達董事會不考慮黃仁勳回鍋
items.summary: A source told CNBC that Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang, pushing back on Financial Times reporting that he was negotiating a return with backing from Silicon Valley figures. The denial matters because much of Monday's hope trade in Asia rested on a quick restoration. Nvidia reports quarterly results this week, its first under interim CEO Colette Kress, and the guidance will set the tone for AI hardware names globally. Analysts have already begun trimming price targets ahead of the print.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic TPU orders extend Google visibility to 2029
items.sub: OpenAI、Anthropic 訂單讓 Google TPU 能見度到 2029
items.summary: Orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended demand visibility for Google's tensor processing units out to 2029, according to supply-chain reporting. The commitments matter as a counterweight to the Nvidia-centric view of AI infrastructure, suggesting large labs are deliberately diversifying their accelerator supply. For Taiwanese suppliers the read-across is mixed: custom-silicon and ASIC design houses benefit from a broader customer base, while the memory and substrate names tied most tightly to GPU cycles stay exposed to swings in a single vendor's roadmap.

items.title: YOASOBI play Taipei Dome on 9 and 10 January 2027
items.sub: YOASOBI 2027/1/9、1/10 登台北大巨蛋
items.summary: YOASOBI will perform two nights at the Taipei Dome on 9 and 10 January 2027, their largest Taiwan shows to date. Tickets are sold through a real-name registration and lottery system rather than first-come sales, so entry depends on the draw rather than queueing speed. The pair are touring behind their recent single run and are expected to include the anime tie-in tracks that broke them internationally. Fans travelling from Hong Kong and Japan are also being accommodated under the same registration scheme.

items.title: Kenshi Yonezu's IRIS OUT holds Billboard anime chart for 17 weeks
items.sub: 米津玄師〈IRIS OUT〉動畫榜 17 連霸
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu's IRIS OUT has now topped Billboard Japan's Hot Animation chart for seventeen consecutive weeks, an unusually long run even by his standards. On the same chart week, King Gnu's new single entered at number two, giving the band their strongest debut placing of the year. The result keeps both acts in heavy rotation going into the year-end award season, where Yonezu is widely expected to feature. His Taipei Dome dates in late December remain the headline Taiwan booking for J-pop fans.

items.title: Mrs. GREEN APPLE map out plans through 2029
items.sub: Mrs. GREEN APPLE 公布至 2029 年計畫
items.summary: Mrs. GREEN APPLE have laid out an unusually long event roadmap, running through 2029. The near-term items include the Ringo Jam Tour 'SHADOWS' fan-club arena run covering 13 cities and 28 performances, followed in 2027 by 'Mrs. GREEN APPLE on Harmony 2' and a dedicated costume exhibition. The band have been steadily expanding the scale of their staging, and the multi-year announcement is designed to let fan-club members plan ballots well in advance. No Taiwan date has been confirmed in the current schedule.

items.title: Vaundy returns to Taipei Arena in 2026 tour leg
items.sub: Vaundy 2026 台北小巨蛋場次實名抽選
items.summary: Vaundy's Taipei Arena show runs under a real-name lottery registration system, with seating maps and price tiers published ahead of the draw. The artist has become one of the most consistently booked Japanese acts in Taiwan, and demand has outstripped capacity at every previous visit. Alongside Vaundy, Yuuri and Fujii Kaze have all made Taipei stops in the current cycle, making this one of the densest years for J-pop touring in the market. Streaming links for the setlist material are available on Spotify.
